title: Word Problems and Number Sentences

standard_text: 2.4D generate and solve problem situations for a given mathematical number sentence involving addition and subtraction of whole numbers within 1,000; 2.7C represent and solve addition and subtraction word problems where unknowns may be any one of the terms in the problem
meta_desc: Free Grade 2 word problem worksheets for Texas TEKS 2.4D and 2.7C: addition and subtraction stories with the unknown in any place and matching number sentences. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Find what you know and what you need; then add or subtract.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Read the story. What do you know? What do you need to find?
  • Joining or putting together: add. Taking away or comparing: subtract.
  • The unknown can be the start, the change or the end. Use ? for the unknown in a number sentence.
  • Check that your answer makes sense in the story.

Examples

Example

Ava had some shells. She found 15 more. Now she has 42.

? + 15 = 42

42 − 15

Answer: 27 shells

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding when you should subtractGives away or how many more usually means subtract.
Using the wrong numbersUnderline the numbers that matter.
Mixing up the whole and the partsThe whole is the total; the parts add up to it.

items.q: A pet store had 31 fish in a tank. The owner put in 36 more fish. How many fish are in the tank now?
items.e: 36 more were added, so add: 31 + 36 = ☐. 31 + 36 = 67. Answer: 67 fish.

items.q: Mia had 50 stickers. She gave 22 stickers to a friend. How many stickers does Mia have now?
items.e: 22 were taken away, so subtract: 50 − 22 = ☐. 50 − 22 = 28. You cannot take 2 from 0 in the ones place, so trade 1 ten for 10 ones first. Answer: 28 stickers.
